362225.title: The induced Thomassen conjecture
362225.literal_statement:
For a graph $G$, write $\delta(G)$ for its minimum degree and $\operatorname{girth}(G)$ for its girth. A graph is **induced-subgraph-free of the two basic obstructions** when it contains neither the relevant clique nor biclique as an induced subgraph. **The induced Thomassen conjecture.** There is a function $g:\mathbb{N}^2\rightarrow\mathbb{N}$ such that for any integers $k$ and $d$, every graph $G$ with $\delta(G)\geq g(k,d)$ has an induced subgraph $H$ for which either $H\cong K_d$, $H\cong K_{d,d}$, or

$$
\delta(H)>d\quad\text{and}\quad \operatorname{girth}(H)>k.
$$

The claim seeks an induced-subgraph analogue of Thomassen's conjecture. The clique and biclique alternatives are necessary because $K_t$ and $K_{t,t}$ have no induced subgraph of minimum degree greater than $1$ and girth greater than $4$.

357495.title: The tree-decomposition minor conjecture
357495.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, let $T$ be a tree, and let $\mathcal{B}$ be the bags of a tree decomposition $(T,\mathcal{B})$ of $G$. The width of this decomposition is the maximum, over all $x\in V(T)$, of $|\{v\in V(G):x\in T_v\}|-1$, and $\operatorname{tw}(G)$ denotes the minimum width of a tree decomposition of $G$. A graph $T$ is a **minor** of $G$ if it can be obtained from $G$ by vertex and edge deletions and edge contractions.

**The tree-decomposition minor conjecture.** There is a function $f$ such that every connected graph $G$ has a tree decomposition $(T,\mathcal{B})$ of width at most $f(\operatorname{tw}(G))$ such that $T$ is a minor of $G$.

The paper states that this conjecture is false, even for connected graphs of treewidth $2$, and uses it as the first of three progressively stronger conjectures in the route to its main theorem.

368044.title: Fleischner–Jackson–Litsyn–Swart's classification conjecture for 2-factor Hamiltonian regular bipartite graphs
368044.literal_statement:
A **2-factor** of a graph is a 2-regular spanning subgraph, and a graph is **2-factor Hamiltonian** if every 2-factor is a Hamiltonian cycle. A **star product** of cubic graphs is the operation that deletes one degree-3 vertex from each graph and joins the resulting three pairs of neighbours. Let $G$ be a 2-factor Hamiltonian $k$-regular bipartite graph.

**Fleischner–Jackson–Litsyn–Swart's conjecture.** Either $k=2$ and $G$ is a cycle, or $k=3$ and $G$ can be obtained from $K_{3,3}$ and the Heawood graph $H_0$ by repeated star products.

The cited work proved that no such graphs exist for $k\geq 4$ and established additional structural restrictions for $k=3$, but the supplied text gives no resolution of the classification conjecture itself.

359218.title: Manvel's eventual reconstructibility conjecture for graphs
359218.literal_statement: For $l\in\mathbb{N}$, let an $l$-deck be the multiset of $l$-vertex induced subgraphs of a graph, and call a graph **$\ell$-reconstructible** if it is determined by its $(n-\ell)$-deck. **Manvel's conjecture.** For $l\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists a threshold $M_\ell$ such that every graph with at least $M_\ell$ vertices is $\ell$-reconstructible. This extends the classical Reconstruction Conjecture from vertex-deleted decks; the paper states that no proof was known for any fixed $\ell$, while the present work studies threshold bounds for special graph classes.

360041.title: The universality conjecture for finite connected graph minor classes
360041.literal_statement:
Let $X$ be a finite connected graph. A graph is **strongly universal** for a class of graphs if every graph in the class appears as a subgraph of it, and **weakly universal** if every graph in the class appears as a minor of it. An $X$-minor-free graph is a graph with no minor isomorphic to $X$.

**Universality conjecture.** The following are equivalent:

$$
\text{There is a strongly universal }X\text{-minor-free graph};
$$

$$
\text{There is a weakly universal }X\text{-minor-free graph};
$$

$$
X\text{ is planar}.
$$

This conjecture would characterize exactly the finite connected graphs whose minor-closed classes admit universal graphs in either sense. The surrounding discussion notes several positive and negative results, but the equivalence is not established in general.

360352.title: The half-breadth internally 4-connected minor conjecture
360352.literal_statement: Let $M$ be a matroid with a tangle $\mathcal{T}$ of order $k\geq 4$ and breadth $m$. **The half-breadth internally 4-connected minor conjecture.** The matroid $M$ has an internally $4$-connected minor $N$ with a tangle $\mathcal{T}'$ of order $k$ such that $\mathcal{T}$ generates $\mathcal{T}'$ in $N$ and the breadth of $\mathcal{T}'$ is at least $m/2$. This would strengthen the weakly $4$-connected outcome available when breadth is preserved exactly, by allowing a controlled loss of breadth; the conjecture is stated as an open problem in the paper.

364771.title: Functional monotonicity conjecture for contraction distance to minor-closed classes
364771.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a minor-closed graph class. For a graph $G$, let $\mathsf{id}_{\mathcal{H}}(G)$ denote the minimum number of edge identifications needed to transform $G$ into a graph in $\mathcal{H}$, and let $\mathsf{ec}_{\mathcal{H}}(G)$ denote the minimum number of edge contractions needed to transform $G$ into a graph in $\mathcal{H}$. **Functional monotonicity conjecture.** There is a function $f_{\mathcal{H}}:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that for every graph $G$, 
$$
\mathsf{ec}_{\mathcal{H}}(G)\leq f_{\mathcal{H}}(\mathsf{id}_{\mathcal{H}}(G)).
$$
 This would extend the displayed polynomial relationship proved in the paper for forests to every minor-closed class, showing that edge-contraction distance is bounded as a function of edge-identification distance; no resolution is given.

369887.title: The two-copy coarse Erdős–Pósa conjecture for planar graphs
369887.literal_statement:
Let $H$ be a planar graph. A **$K$-fat minor-model of $H$** is a $K$-fat model of $H$, and $B_G(Z,cK)$ denotes the ball of radius $cK$ around $Z$ in $G$. Then there exists a constant $c$ such that for every graph $G$, if $G$ does not contain two $K$-fat minor-models of $H$ at distance at least $K$ from each other, then there is a set $Z$ of at most $c$ vertices of $G$ such that $B_G(Z,cK)$ meets all $K$-fat $H$ minor-models in $G$. **Two-copy coarse Erdős–Pósa conjecture.**

The paper states this as the unresolved case of two copies after showing that planar graphs do not generally have the coarse Erdős–Pósa property.

369888.title: The far-apart planar Erdős–Pósa conjecture
369888.literal_statement:
Let $H$ be a planar graph. An **$H$ minor-model** is a model of $H$ in $G$, and minor-models are **pairwise distance at least $d$** when every two distinct models are at that distance or farther. Then there is a function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and a constant $c$ such that for every graph $G$, if $G$ does not contain $n$ disjoint $H$ minor-models that have pairwise distance at least $d$ from each other, then there is a set $Z$ of at most $f(n)$ vertices of $G$ such that $G-B_G(Z,cd)$ contains no $H$ minor. **Far-apart planar Erdős–Pósa conjecture.**

This conjecturally strengthens the known far-apart-cycle result to arbitrary planar minor-models. The paper presents it after contrasting it with the failure of the general coarse Erdős–Pósa property.

375683.title: Erdős–Rubin–Taylor conjecture on non-4-choosable planar graphs
375683.literal_statement: A **planar graph** is a graph that can be drawn in the plane without crossings. A graph is **4-choosable** if every assignment of lists of four colors admits a proper coloring from those lists. **Erdős–Rubin–Taylor's conjecture.** There exists a planar graph which is not 4-choosable. This contrasts with the four-color theorem, which guarantees ordinary 4-colorability for every planar graph; the conjecture was disproved by Voigt's example of a non-4-choosable planar graph.

368251.title: Finite unavoidable-minor conjecture for large-girth matroids
368251.literal_statement:
Let $B(G)$ denote the **bicircular matroid** of a graph $G$, let $U_{t,t+2}$ be the uniform matroid of rank $t$ on $t+2$ elements, and let $M(K_t)$ and $M(K_t)^*$ be respectively the graphic matroid of the complete graph $K_t$ and its dual. **Finite unavoidable-minor conjecture.** There exists a function $g$ such that for every integer $t$, every cosimple matroid with girth at least $g(t)$ contains one of

$$
U_{t,t+2},\quad M(K_t),\quad M(K_t)^*,\quad B(K_t)
$$

as a minor.

362228.title: Logarithmic degree-boundedness for intersection graphs of proper minor-closed classes
362228.literal_statement:
A graph class $\mathcal{F}$ is **proper** if some graph is not isomorphic to any graph in $\mathcal{F}$. Write $int(\mathcal{F})$ for the class of intersection graphs of collections of vertex-subsets inducing connected subgraphs of graphs in $\mathcal{F}$. **Intersection-graph degree conjecture.** For every proper minor-closed class of graphs $\mathcal{F}$, there is a constant $c=c(\mathcal{F})$ such that every graph $G\in int(\mathcal{F})$ has a vertex of degree at most

c\tau(G)\log(\tau(G)).
$$

The conjecture proposes a uniform growth rate for degree-bounding functions of these intersection-graph classes. The source notes that degree-boundedness is known, while this stronger quantitative bound remains open.

370175.title: Directed Burr–Erdős conjecture for oriented hypercubes
370175.literal_statement:
Let $\vv{Q_d}$ denote the oriented $d$-dimensional hypercube, and let $\vv{r}(\vv{Q_d})$ be its oriented Ramsey number. **Directed Burr–Erdős conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that

358722.title: Signed Lovász induced negative cycle conjecture
358722.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a signed graph, let $k$ be a natural number, and call a signed graph **unbalanced** if it contains a negative cycle. An **induced negative cycle** is a negative cycle whose vertices induce no additional edges. A signed graph is $k$-connected if its underlying graph is $k$-connected.

**Signed Lovász conjecture.** For every natural number $k$, there exists a least natural number $f'(k)$ such that, for every $f'(k)$-connected, unbalanced signed graph $G$, there is an induced negative cycle $C$ such that $G-V(C)$ is $k$-connected.

The source presents this as a natural signed-graph generalization of Lovász's induced path connectivity conjecture, obtained by adding a single negative edge between the prescribed vertices. The supplied text gives no resolution status.

373773.title: Bollobás–Meir conjecture for the power-weighted Euclidean traveling-salesman problem
373773.literal_statement:
For a finite set of points $X \subseteq [0,1]^k$, let $S_k(H)=\sum_{e\in H}|e|^k$ for a Hamiltonian cycle $H$ on $X$, and let

$$
S_k^{\mathrm{HC}}(X):=\min_H S_k(H),\qquad S_k^{\mathrm{HC}}:=\sup\{S_k^{\mathrm{HC}}(X):X\subseteq[0,1]^k,\ X\text{ finite}\}.
$$

**Bollobás–Meir conjecture.** For any finite set of points $X\subseteq[0,1]^k$, there exists a Hamiltonian cycle $H$ on $X$ with $S_k(H)\leq 2\cdot k^{k/2}$ if $k\neq3$, and $S_3(H)\leq2^{7/2}$ if $k=3$. Equivalently,

$$
S_k^{\mathrm{HC}}=\begin{cases}2\cdot k^{k/2}&\text{for }k\neq3,\\2^{7/2}&\text{for }k=3.
\end{cases}
$$

The original Bollobás–Meir conjecture asserted the first value for every $k$, but it was disproved in dimension $3$ by Balogh, Clemen and Dumitrescu. The displayed statement is their adjusted conjecture, which remains open for all $k>2$; the cases $k=1,2$ are known.

375528.title: Uniform obstruction-size conjecture for classes of a fixed limiting density
375528.literal_statement: For a graph class $\mathcal{G}$, let $\operatorname{obs}(\mathcal{G})$ denote its minor obstruction set. For a class property $\mathbb{C}$, let $\operatorname{cobs}(\mathbb{C})$ be the set of inclusion-minimal proper minor-closed graph classes not in $\mathbb{C}$. For rational $\delta$, let $\mathbb{C}_{\leq\delta}$ and $\mathbb{C}_{<\delta}$ be the corresponding class properties defined by limiting density. **Uniform obstruction-size conjecture.** There is a constructible function $f:\mathbb{Q}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every $\delta\in\mathbb{Q}$, if $\mathcal{G}\in\operatorname{cobs}(\mathbb{C}_{\leq\delta})$ or $\mathcal{G}\in\operatorname{cobs}(\mathbb{C}_{<\delta})$, then every graph in $\operatorname{obs}(\mathcal{G})$ has at most $f(\delta)$ vertices. This is proposed as a refinement of the finite obstruction conjecture, and its status is open in the supplied text.

376007.title: Coarse Erdős–Pósa conjecture for fat triangle minor-models
376007.literal_statement:
A graph $G$ contains a **$d$-fat minor-model** of $K_3$ when the branch sets and connecting paths satisfy the coarse separation conditions associated with fat minors; write $B_G(X,r)$ for the set of vertices of $G$ at distance at most $r$ from $X$. Two such models are **pairwise at distance more than $d$** when their vertex sets are mutually at distance greater than $d$.

**Coarse Erdős–Pósa conjecture.** There exist functions

$$
f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}\qquad\text{and}\qquad g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N},
$$

with $g(d)\in\mathcal{O}(d)$, such that, for all positive integers $k$ and $d$, and every graph $G$, either $G$ contains $k$ $d$-fat minor-models of $K_3$ that are pairwise at distance more than $d$, or there exists a subset $X$ of vertices of $G$ with $|X|\leqslant f(k)$ such that $G-B_G(X,g(d))$ has no $d$-fat $K_3$ minor-model.

This is a coarse analogue of the Erdős–Pósa theorem, replacing ordinary minor-models by fat minor-models and requiring the models to be far apart. The source reports that a proof was announced in March 2026, but supplies no definitive resolution; the database status therefore remains open pending verification of that announcement.

368138.title: Quasirandomness conjecture for constant-degree tests of stochastic block models
368138.literal_statement:
Let $\mathbb{P}_n$ be a stochastic block model, with parameters allowed to depend arbitrarily on $n$, and let $\mathbb{G}(n,1/2)$ denote the Erdős–Rényi random graph. A **signed subgraph count** is the statistic associated with a signed copy count of a fixed graph, and a **constant-degree polynomial test** is a polynomial test of degree bounded independently of $n$. The hypotheses are

$$
\mathsf{H}_0: \mathbb{G}(n,1/2),\qquad \mathsf{H}_1: \mathbb{P}_n.
$$

**Quasirandomness conjecture.** There exists a constant-degree polynomial test that distinguishes these hypotheses with high probability if and only if one of the signed subgraph counts for an edge, a star, a triangle, or a $4$-cycle distinguishes them with high probability.

This conjecture seeks to extend the preceding star-count result to arbitrary stochastic block models, including models in which conditioning on the latent structure does not force edge probabilities to be at least $1/2$. The paper proves the claim under several structural conditions, including cross-community edge probability exactly $1/2$, all edge probabilities at least $1/2$, community probabilities bounded below by a universal positive constant, or two communities; the general case remains open.
